source.text: וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֹתִ֗י דֶּ֣רֶךְ שַׁ֤עַר הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ הַֽחִיצ֔וֹן הַפֹּנֶ֖ה קָדִ֑ים וְה֖וּא סָגֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought me back [the] way of [the] gate of the sanctuary, the outer, which faces east, and it [was] shut.

en.L: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east; and it was shut.
en.B: Then the man brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
en.R: Then the man took me back to the outer east gate of the temple area. The gate was shut.

decisions.choice: it was shut: the gate by which the glory entered is now closed
decisions.reason: The outer east gate is the one by which the glory of the LORD returned (43:1-4). Verse 2 gives the reason it is shut.

decisions.choice: the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 43:1, the guide is named so that he is not taken for the LORD, who speaks in verse 2.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהוָ֗ה הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַזֶּה֩ סָג֨וּר יִהְיֶ֜ה לֹ֣א יִפָּתֵ֗חַ וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא־יָ֣בֹא ב֔וֹ כִּ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣א ב֑וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה סָגֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to me, This gate shut it will be; it will not be opened, and no one will enter by it, for Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, has entered by it; and it will be shut.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "This gate will remain shut; it will not be opened, and no one will enter by it, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has entered by it. So it will remain shut.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "This gate is to stay shut. It must not be opened, and no one may come in through it, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has come in through it. Therefore it is to stay shut.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "This gate must stay shut. It must never be opened. No one may come in through it, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has come in through it. That is why it must stay shut.

decisions.choice: for the LORD has entered by it: the gate is closed because the LORD used it
decisions.reason: A gate used by the king was closed to others, out of honor. More than that, the LORD who entered by it will not leave again, as he did in 10:19 and 11:23. The shut gate is a sign that his return is for good (43:7, 9).

decisions.choice: this gate shall remain shut: later readings
decisions.reason: The text speaks of the temple's east gate and gives its own reason. In later centuries some Christian writers read the shut gate as a picture of the virgin birth of Christ, and the east gate of Jerusalem's walls, walled up in Ottoman times, has been linked with this verse. Neither reading is in the text itself.

decisions.choice: is to stay shut (B); must stay shut (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "shut it will be" states a lasting rule, which Balanced and Readable make plain.

source.text: אֶֽת־הַנָּשִׂ֗יא נָ֥שִׂיא ה֛וּא יֵֽשֶׁב־בּ֥וֹ לֶאֱכָול־לֶ֖חֶםלִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ אֻלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: The prince, prince he, he will sit in it to eat bread before Yahweh; by [the] way of [the] porch of the gate he will enter, and by its way he will go out.

en.L: [As for] the prince, [because he is] prince, he may sit in it to eat bread before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He will enter by way of the porch of the gate, and by the same way he will go out."
en.B: Only the prince, because he is the prince, may sit in the gateway to eat a meal in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He is to come in by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way."
en.R: Only the ruler may sit inside the gateway, because he is the ruler. He may eat a meal there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He must come in through the porch at the inner end of the gate and go out the same way."

decisions.choice: the prince: the ruler of the restored people
decisions.reason: The word *nasi'* means a leader, one lifted up. Ezekiel uses it for the kings of Judah (12:10; 21:30) and for the coming ruler, "my servant David" (34:24; 37:25). In chapters 44-48 the prince has honor and duties in the worship of the temple, but he is not called king. He is a man: he brings sin offerings for himself (45:22) and has sons who inherit land (46:16). So he is not a figure of God and takes no capital pronouns.

decisions.choice: to eat bread before the LORD: to eat a sacred meal in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: "Bread" means food generally. The prince eats the meal of his peace offerings (46:2, 12) in the gate, as the elders of Israel ate and drank before God on Sinai (Exodus 24:11).

decisions.choice: he will enter by the porch: from inside the outer court
decisions.reason: The prince does not use the shut outer doors. He comes into the gate from the outer court by way of its porch at the inner end (40:8-9), and leaves the same way.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for *nasi'* in chapters 44-48. Readable says "ruler", which says what he does; "prince" today suggests a king's son.

decisions.choice: a meal (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Bread" means food here (m2).

source.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֜נִי דֶּֽרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר הַצָּפוֹן֮ אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבַּיִת֒ וָאֵ֕רֶא וְהִנֵּ֛ה מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶפֹּ֖ל אֶל־פָּנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought me [the] way of [the] gate of the north to [the] face of the house, and I looked, and look, [the] glory of Yahweh filled [the] house of Yahweh, and I fell on my face.

en.L: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house; and I looked, and look, the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] filling the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! And I fell on my face.
en.B: Then the man brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house, and I fell face down.
en.R: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked and saw that the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I bowed down with my face to the ground.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD: as in 43:5
decisions.reason: The words repeat 43:5 and recall Isaiah 6:1-5, where the prophet saw the LORD's glory fill the temple before he received his message. Here too the laws that follow are given in the presence of the glory.

decisions.choice: I fell face down (B); I bowed down with my face to the ground (R)

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהֹוָ֗ה בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם שִׂ֣ים לִבְּךָ֩ וּרְאֵ֨ה בְעֵינֶ֜יךָ וּבְאָזְנֶ֣יךָ שְּׁמָ֗ע אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אֹתָ֔ךְ לְכָל־חֻקּ֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וּלְכָל־תּֽוֹרֹתָ֑יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ לִבְּךָ֙ לִמְב֣וֹא הַבַּ֔יִת בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹצָאֵ֥י הַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to me, Son of man, set your heart and see with your eyes and with your ears hear all that I [am] speaking with you concerning all [the] statutes of [the] house of Yahweh and concerning all its laws; and set your heart to [the] entrance of the house with all [the] exits of the sanctuary.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Son of man, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and with your ears hear all that I am speaking with you concerning all the statutes of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and all its laws; and set your heart on the entrance of the house, with all the exits of the sanctuary.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Son of man, pay close attention. Look carefully and listen closely to everything I tell you about all the statutes and laws of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house. Note carefully who may enter the temple and who must be kept out of the sanctuary.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Son of man, pay careful attention. Watch and listen to everything I tell you about all the laws and teachings for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Note carefully who may come into the temple and who must be kept out of the holy places.

decisions.choice: set your heart and see with your eyes and hear with your ears: as in 40:4
decisions.reason: The LORD repeats the charge the guide gave at the start of the vision (40:4). What follows are the rules for the people who serve in the temple.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the house with all the exits of the sanctuary: who may come in and who must stay out
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces the rules about who may enter the sanctuary and who may not (verses 6-16). Some read "those who may enter" and "those who are excluded".

decisions.choice: who may enter the temple and who must be kept out of the sanctuary (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase refers to (m2).

decisions.choice: statutes ... laws (L, B); laws ... teachings (R)
decisions.reason: As in 43:11.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֶל־מֶ֨רִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רַב־לָכֶ֛ם מִֽכָּל־תּוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to rebellion, to [the] house of Israel, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Enough for you of all your abominations, house of Israel,

en.L: And you will say to the rebellious, to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel,
en.B: Say to the rebellious house of Israel, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Enough of all your detestable practices, house of Israel!
en.R: Say to the people of Israel, who refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: People of Israel, stop all your disgusting practices!

decisions.choice: to rebellion: to the rebellious people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to rebellion", the abstract word for the person, as the book often calls Israel "a house of rebellion" (2:5-8; 12:2-3).

decisions.choice: enough for you: stop now
decisions.reason: The phrase calls a halt, as in 45:9 and Deuteronomy 1:6.

decisions.choice: the rebellious (L); the rebellious house of Israel (B); the people of Israel, who refuse to obey me (R)
decisions.reason: As the book's wording for *bet meri* (2:5), adapted to the form "to rebellion" here.

decisions.choice: abominations (L); detestable practices (B); disgusting practices (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for this word (5:9); Readable says "practices" because these are things done.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: (L); the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: (B); This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: (R)
decisions.reason: The book's formula. The message Ezekiel is to deliver takes no quotation marks of its own.

source.text: בַּהֲבִיאֲכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־נֵכָ֗ר עַרְלֵי־לֵב֙ וְעַרְלֵ֣י בָשָׂ֔ר לִהְי֥וֹת בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לְחַלְּל֣וֹ אֶת־בֵּיתִ֑י בְּהַקְרִֽיבְכֶ֤ם אֶת־לַחְמִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם וַיָּפֵ֨רוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֶ֖ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: in your bringing [the] sons of a foreign land, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, to be in my sanctuary to profane it, my house, when you offer my bread, fat and blood; and they broke my covenant, by all your abominations.

en.L: in your bringing in foreigners, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, to be in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary to profane it, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, when you offered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food, the fat and the blood. And they broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, [in addition] to all your abominations.
en.B: You brought foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, defiling {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple while you offered {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food, the fat and the blood. You broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with all your detestable practices.
en.R: You brought foreigners into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place, people who were not circumcised and who did not love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in their hearts. They made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple unholy while you offered {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} food, the fat and the blood. You broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant by all your disgusting practices.

decisions.choice: foreigners in the sanctuary: non-Israelites used as temple servants
decisions.reason: The first temple had foreign servants: the Gibeonites served at the altar (Joshua 9:23, 27), and foreign guards (the Carites, 2 Kings 11:4-8) stood in the temple. The "temple servants" of Ezra 2:43-58 may have descended from such people. The LORD now forbids it.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh: outside the covenant in both body and will
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:10-14). To be uncircumcised in heart is to be closed to the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4; 9:25).

decisions.choice: and they broke my covenant: the Septuagint and others read "you broke"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they broke", referring to the foreigners or to Israel. The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Latin have "you broke", which fits the rest of the verse. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: my bread, the fat and the blood: the offerings given to the LORD
decisions.reason: The fat and the blood of every sacrifice belonged to the LORD (Leviticus 3:16-17). They are called his "food" as in Leviticus 21:6.

decisions.choice: foreigners (all levels)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "sons of a foreign land", the usual phrase for a foreigner.

decisions.choice: not circumcised and who did not love me in their hearts (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the double phrase (m2), as Jeremiah 9:25 does.

decisions.choice: You broke my covenant (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you" to keep the address to Israel clear; the Hebrew "they" (m3) is footnoted.

source.text: וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת קָדָשָׁ֑י וַתְּשִׂימ֗וּן לְשֹׁמְרֵ֧י מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֛י בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you did not keep [the] charge of my holy things, but you set [them] [as] keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.

en.L: And you have not kept charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things, but you have set [others] to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary for you.
en.B: You have not carried out your duty with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things yourselves, but you have put others in charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary for you.
en.R: You did not take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things yourselves. Instead you put foreigners in charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place.

decisions.choice: keep the charge of my holy things: carry out the duties of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the Levites' and priests' duties (Numbers 3:7-8; 18:3-5). The people had left those duties to foreigners.

decisions.choice: foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: The "others" are the foreigners of verse 7. Readable names them.

source.text: כֹּה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ כָּל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֗ר עֶ֤רֶל לֵב֙ וְעֶ֣רֶל בָּשָׂ֔ר לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֑י לְכָל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֕ר בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Any son of a foreign land, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, will not enter into my sanctuary, of any son of a foreign land who [is] among [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, will enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, of all the foreigners who [are] among the sons of Israel.
en.B: the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, not even one of the foreigners who live among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: No foreigner who is not circumcised and who does not love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} may enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place. This includes the foreigners who live among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: no foreigner may enter my sanctuary: the inner sanctuary is kept for the covenant people and their priests
decisions.reason: The rule concerns serving in the sanctuary, not living among Israel. 47:22-23 gives land to the foreigners who live among Israel. Isaiah 56:3-7 looks forward to foreigners who join themselves to the LORD serving him in his house.

decisions.choice: sons of Israel (L); {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's usual rendering.

source.text: כִּ֣י אִם־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽחֲקוּ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י בִּתְע֤וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּע֣וּ מֵֽעָלַ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But the Levites who went far from me, when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols, they will bear their iniquity.

en.L: But the Levites who went far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when Israel strayed, who strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} after their filthy idols, they will bear their iniquity.
en.B: But the Levites who moved far from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when Israel went astray and who strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} after their idols, must bear the consequences of their sin.
en.R: The Levites left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when the people of Israel turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to follow their idols. Now they must suffer the results of their sin.

decisions.choice: the Levites who went far from me: Levites who served at the high places and idol shrines
decisions.reason: When Josiah closed the high places, their priests were brought to Jerusalem but not allowed to serve at the altar (2 Kings 23:8-9). Ezekiel's rule matches this: Levites who led worship away from the LORD are kept from the altar and given other work in the temple (verses 11-14).

decisions.choice: they shall bear their iniquity: they must bear the consequences of their sin
decisions.reason: The phrase means to carry the guilt and its penalty (Leviticus 5:1; Numbers 18:23).

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for *gillulim* (6:4).

decisions.choice: bear the consequences of their sin (B); suffer the results of their sin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bear their iniquity"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2).

source.text: וְהָי֤וּ בְמִקְדָּשִׁי֙ מְשָׁ֣רְתִ֔ים פְּקֻדּוֹת֙ אֶל־שַׁעֲרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וּֽמְשָׁרְתִ֖ים אֶת־הַבָּ֑יִת הֵ֠מָּה יִשְׁחֲט֨וּ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַזֶּ֨בַח֙ לָעָ֔ם וְהֵ֛מָּה יַעַמְד֥וּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָֽׁרְתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will be in my sanctuary ministers, [having] oversight at [the] gates of the house, and ministering to the house; they will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before them to serve them.

en.L: And they will be in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary [as] ministers, overseers at the gates of the house, ministering to the house. They will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before them to serve them.
en.B: They may serve in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary as guards at the gates of the temple and as its servants. They may slaughter the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for the people and stand before the people to serve them.
en.R: They may still work in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple. They may guard its gates and do the work of the temple. They may kill the animals for the people's burnt offerings and sacrifices, and they may serve the people.

decisions.choice: they shall stand before them to serve them: they serve the people, not the LORD at the altar
decisions.reason: The phrase "stand before" someone means to serve him. These Levites stand before the people; only the sons of Zadok "stand before" the LORD (verse 15). The contrast is the point of the passage.

source.text: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְשָׁרְת֤וּ אוֹתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עָוֺ֑ן עַל־כֵּן֩ נָשָׂ֨אתִי יָדִ֜י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Because they served them before their idols and became to [the] house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have raised my hand against them, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, and they will bear their iniquity.

en.L: Because they ministered to them before their filthy idols and became to the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand [in an oath] against them, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and they will bear their iniquity.
en.B: Because they served the people in front of their idols and made the house of Israel stumble into sin, I have raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand in an oath against them, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and they must bear the consequences of their sin.
en.R: They served the people in front of their idols and led the people of Israel into sin. So I have made a solemn promise to punish them, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. They must suffer the results of their sin.

decisions.choice: I have raised my hand against them: I have sworn an oath against them
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of an oath (20:5-6; Genesis 14:22). Here the oath is one of judgment.

decisions.choice: a stumbling block of iniquity: something that makes people fall into sin
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 7:19 and 14:3-7 for idols. The Levites who served at the idols became such a stumbling block themselves.

decisions.choice: [in an oath] (L); in an oath (B); made a solemn promise (R)
decisions.reason: As 20:5 at each level (m1).

source.text: וְלֹֽא־יִגְּשׁ֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לְכַהֵ֣ן לִ֔י וְלָגֶ֨שֶׁת֙ עַל־כָּל־קָ֣דָשַׁ֔י אֶל־קָדְשֵׁ֖י הַקְּדָשִׁ֑ים וְנָֽשְׂאוּ֙ כְּלִמָּתָ֔ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will not come near to me to serve as priest to me, and to come near to all my holy things, to the most holy things; and they will bear their shame and their abominations which they did.

en.L: And they will not come near to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests, nor come near to any of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things, to the most holy things; and they will bear their shame and [the consequences of] their abominations that they have done.
en.B: They are not to approach {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests, nor to approach any of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things or the most holy offerings. They must bear their disgrace for the detestable practices they committed.
en.R: They must not come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to serve as priests. They must not touch any of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy things or the most holy offerings. They must suffer shame because of the disgusting things they did.

decisions.choice: not come near to serve as priests: they may not offer at the altar or enter the holy place
decisions.reason: Coming near the LORD, to the altar and the holy things, was the priest's right alone (Numbers 18:3-7). These Levites keep the work of the gates and the courts but lose this privilege.

decisions.choice: [the consequences of] (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "bear ... their abominations" means bearing the shame and the penalty of them.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַבָּ֑יִת לְכֹל֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ וּלְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will make them keepers of [the] charge of the house, for all its service and for all that will be done in it.

en.L: And I will appoint them to keep the charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is to be done in it.
en.B: Yet I will put them in charge of the duties of the temple, all its work and everything that has to be done in it.
en.R: But I will put them in charge of taking care of the temple. They will do all its work and everything that needs to be done there.

source.text: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י צָד֗וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְר֜וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ בִּתְע֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י הֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֵלַ֖י לְשָֽׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְעָמְד֣וּ לְפָנַ֗י לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priests the Levites, [the] sons of Zadok, who kept [the] charge of my sanctuary when [the] sons of Israel went astray from me, they will come near to me to serve me and they will stand before me to offer to me fat and blood, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary when the sons of Israel strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they will come near to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to minister to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they will stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to offer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the fat and the blood, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But the Levitical priests, the descendants of Zadok, who carried out the duties of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} strayed from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, are to come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are to stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to offer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the fat and the blood, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But the priests from the tribe of Levi who are descendants of Zadok stayed faithful and took care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So they may come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They may stand in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to offer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the fat and the blood of the sacrifices, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok: the Jerusalem priesthood
decisions.reason: See 40:46 and 43:19. The sons of Zadok had served in the Jerusalem temple, while other Levites served at the high places (verse 10). In 1 Samuel 2:35 a faithful priest is promised to replace the house of Eli; 1 Kings 2:27, 35 sees this fulfilled in Zadok.

decisions.choice: who kept charge of my sanctuary when Israel went astray: the reason for their honor
decisions.reason: The text does not say the Zadokites were without fault; chapter 8 shows idolatry in the Jerusalem temple itself, and 22:26 condemns its priests. The point is that they kept the LORD's sanctuary, while others led worship away from it.

decisions.choice: the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok (L); the descendants of Zadok (B, R)
stayed faithful (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what keeping charge of the sanctuary meant at that time (m2).

source.text: הֵ֜מָּה יָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֗י וְהֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֶל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י לְשָׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְשָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: They will enter my sanctuary, and they will come near to my table to serve me, and they will keep my charge.

en.L: They [are the ones who] will enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary, and they will approach {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table to minister to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge.
en.B: They alone are to enter {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary and come near {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} service.
en.R: Only they may come into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy place and come near {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They will do the work I give them.

decisions.choice: my table: the altar, or the table of 41:22
decisions.reason: "My table" may be the altar of burnt offering (as Malachi 1:7, 12) or the table that is "before the LORD" in the main hall (41:22).

decisions.choice: alone (B); only (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "they", in contrast with the Levites of verses 10-14.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּבוֹאָם֙ אֶֽל־שַׁעֲרֵי֙ הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔ית בִּגְדֵ֥י פִשְׁתִּ֖ים יִלְבָּ֑שׁוּ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֤ה עֲלֵיהֶם֙ צֶ֔מֶר בְּשָֽׁרְתָ֗ם בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֛י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖ית וָבָֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when they enter [the] gates of the court the inner, garments of linen they will put on, and wool will not come on them when they serve in [the] gates of the court the inner and within.

en.L: And it will be, when they enter the gates of the inner court, they will put on linen garments; no wool will be on them while they minister at the gates of the inner court and within.
en.B: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they must wear linen clothes. They must have nothing made of wool on them while they serve at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple.
en.R: When they come through the gates of the inner courtyard, they must wear linen clothes. They must not wear anything made of wool while they serve at the gates of the inner courtyard or inside the temple.

decisions.choice: linen garments: the priests' sacred clothing
decisions.reason: The law prescribed linen for the priests' garments (Exodus 28:39-43; Leviticus 16:4). Linen is light and cool; wool makes one sweat (verse 18).

decisions.choice: and within: inside the temple building
decisions.reason: The word may mean inside the inner court or inside the temple itself.

source.text: פַּאֲרֵ֤י פִשְׁתִּים֙ יִהְי֣וּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔ם וּמִכְנְסֵ֣י פִשְׁתִּ֔ים יִהְי֖וּ עַל־מָתְנֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א יַחְגְּר֖וּ בַּיָּֽזַע׃

records.literal_gloss: Turbans of linen will be on their head, and undergarments of linen will be on their loins; they will not gird themselves with sweat.

en.L: Linen turbans will be on their heads, and linen undergarments will be on their loins; they will not gird themselves with [anything that causes] sweat.
en.B: Linen turbans are to be on their heads and linen undergarments on their hips; they must not put on anything that makes them sweat.
en.R: They must wear linen turbans on their heads and linen underwear around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

decisions.choice: linen undergarments: as in the law
decisions.reason: The priests' undergarments of Exodus 28:42 were "to cover their nakedness" when they served at the altar.

decisions.choice: not with sweat: nothing that brings bodily impurity
decisions.reason: Sweat was not unclean in the law, but the rule keeps anything of human toil and effort out of the holy place, as tools were kept off the altar (Exodus 20:25). Genesis 3:19 links sweat with the curse on the ground.

source.text: וּ֠בְצֵאתָם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֨ר הַחִיצוֹנָ֜ה אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִיצוֹנָה֮ אֶל־הָעָם֒ יִפְשְׁט֣וּ אֶת־בִּגְדֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֨מָּה֙ מְשָׁרְתִ֣ם בָּ֔ם וְהִנִּ֥יחוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בְּלִֽשְׁכֹ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְלָֽבְשׁוּ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם בְּבִגְדֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And when they go out into the court the outer, into the court the outer to the people, they will strip off their garments in which they were serving, and they will put them in [the] rooms of holiness, and they will put on other garments; and they will not make holy the people with their garments.

en.L: And when they go out into the outer court, into the outer court to the people, they will take off their garments in which they have been ministering and lay them in the holy chambers; and they will clothe themselves in other garments, so that they do not make the people holy by their garments.
en.B: When they go out to the people in the outer court, they must take off the clothes they wore while they served and leave them in the holy rooms. They must put on other clothes, so that they do not pass on holiness to the people through their clothes.
en.R: When they go out to the people in the outer courtyard, they must take off the clothes they wore while serving. They must leave them in the holy rooms and put on other clothes. Otherwise the holiness of their clothes might pass to the people.

decisions.choice: they shall not make the people holy by their garments: holiness could pass by contact
decisions.reason: Holiness, like uncleanness, was thought of as passing from one thing to another by touch (Exodus 29:37; 30:29; Leviticus 6:20). People made holy by accident would be under the rules for holy things, with all their dangers (Haggai 2:12). See 42:14 and 46:20.

decisions.choice: into the outer court, into the outer court: a repeated phrase
decisions.reason: The phrase is written twice in the Hebrew; the Septuagint and some manuscripts have it once. The repetition may be a copying slip.

decisions.choice: pass on holiness (B); the holiness ... might pass (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the clothes could make the people holy (m1).

source.text: וְרֹאשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ וּפֶ֖רַע לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ כָּס֥וֹם יִכְסְמ֖וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And their head they will not shave, and [their] hair they will not let grow long; they will surely trim their heads.

en.L: And they will not shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long; they will only trim [the hair of] their heads.
en.B: They must neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long; they must keep their hair trimmed.
en.R: They must not shave their heads, and they must not let their hair grow long. They must keep it neatly trimmed.

decisions.choice: neither shaved nor long: hair kept in moderation
decisions.reason: Shaving the head was a sign of mourning (7:18; Leviticus 21:5), and letting hair hang loose or long was also a mourning custom (Leviticus 10:6; 21:10). The priests are to avoid both extremes and keep their hair trimmed.

source.text: וְיַ֥יִן לֹֽא־יִשְׁתּ֖וּ כָּל־כֹּהֵ֑ן בְּבוֹאָ֖ם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And wine will not drink any priest when they enter into the court the inner.

en.L: And no priest will drink wine when they enter the inner court.
en.B: No priest may drink wine when he is to enter the inner court.
en.R: No priest may drink wine before going into the inner courtyard.

decisions.choice: no wine before entering the inner court: as Leviticus 10:9
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the same rule to Aaron after the death of his sons Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10:1-9).

decisions.choice: he (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they" refers to each priest; Balanced uses "he", since priests were men.

source.text: וְאַלְמָנָה֙ וּגְרוּשָׁ֔ה לֹֽא־יִקְח֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּ֣י אִם־בְּתוּלֹ֗ת מִזֶּ֨רַע֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה מִכֹּהֵ֖ן יִקָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a widow and a divorced woman they will not take for themselves as wives, but virgins of [the] offspring of [the] house of Israel, and the widow who will be a widow of a priest they may take.

en.L: And they will not take for themselves as wives a widow or a divorced woman, but [only] virgins of the seed of Israel's house; or a widow who is a priest's widow they may take.
en.B: They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of Israelite descent, or a widow whose husband was a priest.
en.R: They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman. They may marry only a young woman of Israelite family who has never been married, or the widow of a priest.

decisions.choice: whom the priests may marry: stricter than the general rule for priests
decisions.reason: Leviticus 21:7 forbade any priest to marry a divorced woman, and 21:13-14 forbade the high priest to marry a widow. Ezekiel applies the high priest's rule to all the priests, but allows the widow of a priest.

decisions.choice: a young woman who has never been married (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "virgins" means here.

source.text: וְאֶת־עַמִּ֣י יוֹר֔וּ בֵּ֥ין קֹ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹ֑ל וּבֵין־טָמֵ֥א לְטָה֖וֹר יוֹדִעֻֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my people they will teach [the difference] between holy and common, and [the difference] between unclean and clean they will make known to them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people they will teach [the difference] between holy and common, and make known to them [the difference] between the unclean and the clean.
en.B: They are to teach {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people the difference between what is holy and what is common, and show them how to tell the unclean from the clean.
en.R: They must teach {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people the difference between what is holy and what is not holy. They must show them how to tell what is unclean from what is clean.

decisions.choice: teach the difference between the holy and the common: the priests' duty from Leviticus 10:10-11
decisions.reason: In 22:26 Ezekiel charged the priests with failing to do this. The new priests will do what the old did not.

decisions.choice: what is holy and what is not holy (R)
decisions.reason: As Leviticus 10:10 at Readable.

source.text: וְעַל־רִ֗יב הֵ֚מָּה יַעַמְד֣וּ לְמִשְׁפָּ֔ט בְּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י יִשְׁפְּט֑וּהוּוְאֶת־תּוֹרֹתַ֤י וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ בְּכָל־מוֹעֲדַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֔רוּ וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֖י יְקַדֵּֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And over a dispute they will stand to judge; by my judgments they will judge it; and my laws and my statutes in all my appointed feasts they will keep, and my Sabbaths they will make holy.

en.L: And in a dispute they will stand to judge; by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments they will judge it. And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes they will keep at all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} appointed feasts, and they will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths holy.
en.B: In a dispute they are to act as judges and decide it according to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings. They are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes at all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} appointed festivals, and they are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths holy.
en.R: When people have a dispute, the priests must act as judges. They must decide the case by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. They must obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teachings and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws at all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} festivals, and they must keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days holy.

decisions.choice: the priests as judges: as Deuteronomy 17:8-9
decisions.reason: Hard cases were brought to "the Levitical priests" and the judge at the sanctuary (Deuteronomy 17:8-13; 19:17; 21:5).

decisions.choice: to judge: the written text and the reading tradition differ slightly
decisions.reason: The written text has "for judgment" and the reading tradition "to judge"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: judgments (L); rulings (B); rules (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for *mishpatim* (5:6).

decisions.choice: laws and statutes (L, B); teachings and laws (R)
decisions.reason: As in 43:11: *torot* is "laws" (L, B) and "teachings" (R); *chuqqot* is "statutes" (L, B) and "laws" (R).

source.text: וְאֶל־מֵ֣ת אָדָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא לְטָמְאָ֑ה כִּ֣י אִם־לְאָ֡ב וּ֠לְאֵם וּלְבֵ֨ן וּלְבַ֜ת לְאָ֗ח וּלְאָח֛וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה לְאִ֖ישׁ יִטַּמָּֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to a dead person he will not go to become unclean, but for father or for mother or for son or for daughter, for brother or for sister who has not been to a husband, they may become unclean.

en.L: And [a priest] will not go near a dead person to become unclean; but for a father, or for a mother, or for a son, or for a daughter, for a brother, or for a sister who has not had a husband, they may become unclean.
en.B: A priest must not make himself unclean by going near a dead body. But he may make himself unclean for his father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or a sister who had no husband.
en.R: A priest must not go near a dead body, because it would make him unclean. But he may do so if the dead person is his father or mother, his son or daughter, his brother, or his sister who was not married.

decisions.choice: contact with the dead: as Leviticus 21:1-3
decisions.reason: Touching a dead body made a person unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:11). The law allowed a priest to become unclean only for his closest relatives (Leviticus 21:1-3).

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵ֖י טָֽהֳרָת֑וֹ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים יִסְפְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And after his cleansing, seven days they will count for him.

en.L: And after he is cleansed, they will count seven days for him.
en.B: After he has been cleansed, he must wait seven more days.
en.R: After he has become clean again, he must wait seven more days.

decisions.choice: seven days after his cleansing: a further week before he serves
decisions.reason: The cleansing itself took seven days (Numbers 19:11-12). Ezekiel adds a further seven days before the priest may serve again (verse 27).

source.text: וּבְיוֹם֩ בֹּא֨וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ יַקְרִ֖יב חַטָּאת֑וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] day he enters into the holy place, into the court the inner, to serve in the holy place, he will offer his sin offering, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And on the day that he enters the holy place, into the inner court, to minister in the holy place, he will offer his sin offering, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: When he enters the sanctuary again, into the inner court, to serve in the sanctuary, he must offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: On the day he goes back into the inner courtyard to serve in the holy place, he must offer a sin offering for himself, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְֽנַחֲלָ֔ה אֲנִ֖י נַֽחֲלָתָ֑ם וַאֲחֻזָּ֗ה לֹֽא־תִתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲנִ֖י אֲחֻזָּתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be for them for an inheritance: I [am] their inheritance; and a possession you will not give to them in Israel: I [am] their possession.

en.L: And this will be their inheritance: I [am] their inheritance. And no possession will you give them in Israel: I [am] their possession.
en.B: Their inheritance is to be this: I am their inheritance. You are not to give them property in Israel; I am their property.
en.R: The priests will not receive any land as their own. I am all they will receive. You must not give them any land in Israel. I myself am what belongs to them.

decisions.choice: I am their inheritance: as Numbers 18:20 and Deuteronomy 18:1-2
decisions.reason: The LORD told Aaron, "I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel" (Numbers 18:20). The priests live from the offerings (verses 29-30) and have land set apart only for their homes (45:4; 48:10-12).

decisions.choice: it will be for them for an inheritance: the Septuagint reads "they shall have no inheritance"
decisions.reason: The Septuagint and the Latin read "they shall have no inheritance", which differs from the Hebrew by one word and matches the second half of the verse. The sense is the same: the LORD himself is their share.

decisions.choice: possession (L); property (B); land ... what belongs to them (R)
decisions.reason: The word *'achuzzah* is "holding" in the chapters on the land (45-48); here it is set beside "inheritance", and each level uses a word that makes the contrast plain.

decisions.choice: The priests will not receive any land as their own. I am all they will receive. (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the saying means (m1).

source.text: הַמִּנְחָה֙ וְהַחַטָּ֣את וְהָאָשָׁ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה יֹֽאכְל֑וּם וְכָל־חֵ֥רֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָהֶ֥ם יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The grain offering and the sin offering and the guilt offering, they will eat them; and every devoted thing in Israel will be theirs.

en.L: The grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering they will eat; and every devoted thing in Israel will be theirs.
en.B: They are to eat the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering, and everything in Israel devoted to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is to be theirs.
en.R: The grain offerings, the sin offerings and the guilt offerings will be their food. Everything in Israel that is given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for good will belong to them.

decisions.choice: every devoted thing: anything given wholly and finally to the LORD
decisions.reason: A "devoted thing" was given to the LORD for good and could not be bought back. Numbers 18:14 gives such things to the priests (Leviticus 27:28).

decisions.choice: devoted to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} (B); given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for good (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say to whom such things were devoted (m1).

source.text: וְרֵאשִׁית֩ כָּל־בִּכּ֨וּרֵי כֹ֜ל וְכָל־תְּר֣וּמַת כֹּ֗ל מִכֹּל֙ תְּרוּמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְרֵאשִׁ֤ית עֲרִסֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ תִּתְּנ֣וּ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן לְהָנִ֥יחַ בְּרָכָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] first of all [the] firstfruits of everything, and every contribution of everything, from all your contributions, will be for the priests; and [the] first of your dough you will give to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on your house.

en.L: And the first of all the firstfruits of every kind, and every contribution of every kind from all your contributions, will belong to the priests. And you will give the first of your dough to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on your house.
en.B: The best of all the firstfruits of every kind and every special gift of every kind from all your gifts will belong to the priests. You are also to give the priest the first portion of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your household.
en.R: The priests will receive the best of all the first crops, and every kind of special gift you bring. Also give the priest the first part of the dough you make. Then I will bless your household.

decisions.choice: firstfruits and contributions: the priests' share, as Numbers 18:12-13
decisions.reason: The firstfruits of grain, wine and oil and the gifts set apart for the LORD were given to the priests (Numbers 18:8-19).

decisions.choice: the first of your dough: as Numbers 15:20-21
decisions.reason: Israel was to set apart a loaf from the first batch of dough. The word for dough is rare (Numbers 15:20-21; Nehemiah 10:38).

decisions.choice: contribution: something set apart and given to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word *terumah* comes from a verb meaning "to lift off" or "set apart". It names a gift taken off and given to the LORD. In 45:1 and 48:8-21 the same word is used for the portion of land set apart.

decisions.choice: contribution (L); special gift (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "contribution", the word it uses for *terumah* in 45-48; Balanced and Readable say "special gift" here, where it means an offering, not land.

decisions.choice: Then I will bless your household (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who gives the blessing; the Hebrew says the gift "causes a blessing to rest".

source.text: כָּל־נְבֵלָה֙ וּטְרֵפָ֔ה מִן־הָע֖וֹף וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לֹ֥א יֹאכְל֖וּ הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Any carcass and torn animal, of the birds and of the animals, the priests will not eat.

en.L: The priests will not eat anything, bird or animal, that has died of itself or been torn [by beasts].
en.B: The priests must not eat anything, whether bird or animal, that has died of itself or been killed by wild animals.
en.R: The priests must not eat any bird or animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals.

decisions.choice: carcass and torn animal: as Leviticus 22:8
decisions.reason: Such meat made the eater unclean (Leviticus 11:39-40; 17:15). Ezekiel himself had never eaten it (4:14).

decisions.choice: the end of the chapter: the LORD's speech continues
decisions.reason: The speech that began in 44:5 runs on through chapters 45 and 46 to 46:18, where the narrative resumes in 46:19.

decisions.choice: quotation marks run on (all levels)
decisions.reason: The quotation opened in 44:5 is not closed at the end of this chapter, because the LORD's speech continues to 46:18.
